title: Robust HTTP Event Reassembly and Backoff Protocol for Streaming Responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Clients intermittently lose SSE connections during long-running responses (tool calls, structured JSON partials). Current reconnect behavior sometimes produces duplicate function-call side effects, garbled partial JSON, or stalls when the server switches model backends. Goal: Define and implement a robust HTTP event reassembly protocol and client-server backoff strategy that provides: idempotent resume semantics, clear chunk boundaries for structured outputs and function-call transcripts, graceful partial-output rehydration, and a compatibility header that enables gradual rollout across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Server and client support an epoched resume token that uniquely identifies stream + model variant + server generation
Chunk format includes a monotonic sequence number and explicit boundary token for function-call and JSON object fragments
Reconnect flow guarantees at-most-once invocation semantics for server-side tools when client presents an idempotency token
Clients can request partial reassembly of the last N chunks to repair corrupted JSON without re-requesting the entire response
Protocol versioning via header X-Redwood-Stream-Version and runtime feature negotiation implemented in hosted and Dedicated runtimes
Observability: metrics and logs exposed for resume success rate, duplicate-invocation incidents, and average reassembly latency
implementation_notes: Chunk envelope: UTF-8 text line with 'event: chunk' and data payload containing base64 of protobuf fragment OR raw UTF-8 for structured JSON parts

Envelope fields carried in each chunk: stream_id (uuid), epoch (int), seq (int, monotonic), checksum (crc32), fragment_type (text | json_fragment | function_call | checkpoint), continuation_hint (bool)
Resume token (opaque): base64(url-safe) of [stream_id | epoch | last_ack_seq | server_generation | signature], signed by runtime private key to prevent token forgery
Idempotency: client supplies per-request idempotency_key header for tool calls; server maps seen idempotency_key -> tool-invocation-result TTL 24h
Reassembly: client requests 'rehydrate?from_seq=K' to receive up to N subsequent chunks; server can reply with compact checkpoint chunk representing full reconstructed JSON up to seq M
Backoff: client uses exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (min 200ms, base 500ms, max 10s) for reconnects, escalates to 'fast-fail' when consecutive resume failures >3
Compatibility: negotiate by sending X-Redwood-Stream-Version: 2 in initial request; server may reply X-Redwood-Stream-Features: rehydrate,checkpointing,idempotent-tools
Failure modes: corrupted chunk checksum -> client requests last_good_seq; server offers 'repair' stream where it replays from last_good_seq as read-only
Streaming SDK: add helpers to parse fragment boundaries, assemble JSON tokens incrementally, and surface deterministic function-call completion events to callers
Security: resume token signed, tokens short-lived (1h) for hosted; Dedicated/Private may configure longer TTLs; clients must use TLS and enforce origin checks
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Proposal drafted, initial API sketch and chunk envelope defined. Assigned to Mateo.
2025-02-12: Spike completed - PoC server reassembly endpoint that returns checkpoint chunk. Observed 12% reduction in retransmit bandwidth vs naive replay.
2025-02-14: SDK parsing helpers prototyped in node and python. Edge case found: nested JSON arrays crossing chunk boundaries cause parser to stall; added continuation_hint to envelope.
2025-02-16: Security reviewed resume token signing approach with cryptography team; requested HSM integration notes for Private deployments.
2025-02-18: Design doc updated with backoff defaults and observability metrics. Preparing PR for runtime changes (server-side chunking + resume handling).
decisions: Use epoch + seq resume token rather than byte-offset to tolerate backend model restarts and chunk recomposition.
Support hybrid chunk payloads: raw UTF-8 for small JSON fragments, base64-encoded protobuf for binary-safe fragments.
Require client idempotency_key header for any request that may trigger tool/function invocation. At-most-once guarantee relies on server-side idempotency map.
Expose explicit capability headers instead of implicit feature-flags in payload to allow phased rollout across Dedicated/private customers.
reviewer_feedback: Lina Hu: Favor the epoch approach; please clarify server generation semantics and how we invalidate old resume tokens during deployments.
Rajesh Singh: Add metrics for 'rehydrate_success_rate' and label by customer_tier (hosted vs dedicated). Consider exposing a debug endpoint to dump reassembly state for troubleshooting.
Design: Avoid client-side automatic full-replay for large responses; prefer compact checkpointing to reduce costs for high-throughput customers.
risks: If resume tokens leak, a replay attacker could attempt to enumerate stream state. Mitigation: short TTL and signed tokens.
Stateful idempotency map grows for high QPS customers; need eviction and sharding strategies to avoid memory blowup.
Different client SDK implementations may interpret fragment edges differently leading to compatibility bugs; thorough cross-language tests required.
